title: The Myth of a Global Antifa
author: John Feffer
content:
[![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/IMG_6047.jpeg)](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/08/07/the-
myth-of-a-global-antifa/)

![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/IMG_6047.jpeg)

Global Antifa is a myth. Global fascism and Neo-Nazism aren't. Fascist
graffiti on the wall of a county government building in Clackamas County,
Oregon. Photo: Jeffrey St. Clair.

In September 2025, Donald Trump
[designated](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-
actions/2025/09/designating-antifa-as-a-domestic-terrorist-organization/
"designated") “antifa” a domestic terror organization. Last month, his
administration went one step further by declaring that the “extreme left” had
developed the antifa network into a global threat. Marco Rubio announced at a
press conference on July 16 that

> Antifa militants and their comrades travel from across Europe and to the
> Americas to participate in each other’s attacks, to funnel propaganda and
> training, materials, and target information through shared encrypted
> channels — moving through underground networks of safe houses, and finance
> and sustain their operations through transnational funds.

This description sounds eerily like what global far-right networks have been
doing for years. The “antidem” network, crisscrossing the Atlantic and ranging
up and down the Americas, has helped far-right politicians take over parties,
those parties take power, and those resulting governments coordinate anti-
immigrant, anti-climate, anti-LGBT, and fundamentally anti-democratic
policies. This effort is well-funded by right-wing sugar daddies like [Elon
Musk](https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/elon-musk/elon-musk-boosting-far-right-
politics-globe-rcna189505 "Elon Musk") and [Robert
Shillman](https://www.ftm.eu/articles/geert-wilders-american-patron "Robert
Shillman").

In the United States, even more extreme right-wing militants [have been
responsible](https://www.csis.org/analysis/left-wing-terrorism-and-political-
violence-united-states-what-data-tells-us "have been responsible") for 152
attacks and 112 deaths between 2016 and 2025, compared to 35 attacks and 13
deaths by the extreme left (according to the right-leaning Center for
Strategic and International Studies.

Fascism, not anti-fascism, is the threat, both domestically and
internationally.

It’s a common Trumpian tactic: to blame adversaries for that which the accuser
has perfected. Thus, according to Trump, his enemies are [always
lying](https://www.cnn.com/2025/11/19/politics/donald-trump-lies-false-claims
"always lying"); they’re [completely corrupt](https://omar.house.gov/media/in-
the-news/trump-calls-me-crooked-hell-thats-rich-coming-him "completely
corrupt"); they [are anti-
democratic](https://www.c-span.org/clip/campaign-2024/trump-claims-democrats-
are-real-threat-to-democracy/5132995 "are anti-democratic"). This from the
most mendacious, corrupt, and anti-democratic force in modern politics.
Remember [the canard](https://www.npr.org/2021/03/02/972564176/antifa-didnt-
storm-the-capitol-just-ask-the-rioters "the canard") that it was actually
“antifa” that caused all the havoc during the obviously right-wing
insurrection on January 6? What better way to throw people off the scent of a
vast right-wing conspiracy than to assert that something much more sinister is
percolating on the left.

In practice, the administration is engaged in a category error. It assumes
that organized opposition presupposes an organization. But, as Gertrude Stein
once said rather cruelly of her hometown of Oakland, there’s no “there” there.
Fascism has experienced a successful rebrand in the age of Trump. Lots of
people and institutions are organizing against this fascism. But what the
Trump administration calls “antifa” just doesn’t exist.

**The Antifa that Isn’t**

Understood broadly, anti-fascist forces defeated Hitler, Mussolini, and their
various axis partners. Those forces would eventually include everything from
the U.S. government to the Red Army to underground resistance movements.
Later, such forces helped to suppress fascist parties in Germany. They
challenged white supremacist and neo-Nazi formations in the United States.
Anti-fascist movements saved democracy and then made it stronger.

But that’s not the “antifa” that the Trump administration has in mind. True,
Vice President JD Vance has
[berated](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/02/14/us/politics/vance-far-right-
germany-munich-afd.html "berated") German politicians for refusing to partner
politically with the far-right Alternative for Germany party. And the Trump
administration has [pursued a legal vendetta](https://www.aclu.org/news/free-
speech/trump-administration-attack-on-southern-poverty-law-center-puts-
democracy-at-risk "pursued a legal vendetta") against the Southern Poverty Law
Center, one of the premier U.S. organizations that has gone after the Ku Klux
Klan and similar organizations.

But in invoking the “antifa” rubric, Rubio and company have a somewhat
narrower focus. They [have labeled](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-
actions/2025/09/countering-domestic-terrorism-and-organized-political-
violence/ "have labeled") several discrete assassinations (of far-right youth
leader Charlie Kirk and health care CEO Brian Thompson), attempted
assassinations (of Donald Trump), and plots to assassinate (Supreme Court
Justice Brett Kavanagh) as the work of this shadowy organization. Perhaps more
to the point, the administration has been looking for ways to discredit the
protestors and the organizations who have challenged the administration’s mass
deportation campaign.

In June, the Justice Department [celebrated the
conviction](https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/leader-antifa-cell-members-north-
texas-sentenced-100-years-prison-terrorist-attack-ice "celebrated the
conviction") of “eight North Texas Antifa Cell operatives” for their
involvement in a protest outside an ICE detention facility in Texas. One
police officer was injured in the incident. The man accused of shooting the
officer received a sentence of 100 years in prison. Another defendant, charged
with “transporting a box containing numerous Antifa materials” and trying to
conceal what was in reality a box of his belongings that included some
political zines, [received a sentence of 30
years](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/1/seven-more-sentenced-over-
texas-ice-detention-centre-shooting "received a sentence of 30 years").

Credit the severity of the sentencing with the Justice Department’s tactic of
calling the protests the acts of antifa terrorists. To make this case, the
Justice Department lawyers employed the services of Kyle Shideler, who [works
for the Center for Security
Policy](https://theintercept.com/2026/03/09/prairieland-antifa-ice-protest-
frank-gaffney-islamophobic/ "works for the Center for Security Policy"). This
is the outfit founded by Frank Gaffney, a notorious far-right fabulist who
used Islamophobia as rocket fuel to ascend to infamy.

On the stand, Shideler frankly made a fool of himself by lecturing the judge
and jury about the origins of antifa only to fall apart under the questioning
of defense attorney Patrick McLain. Here’s [Zoe Chase’s
account](https://www.thisamericanlife.org/891/transcript "Zoe Chase’s
account") for _This American Life_ :

> McLain approaches, asks some questions about Shideler’s credentials for
> this, pointing out he’s never held a position at a college or a university.
> He’s never published a peer-reviewed paper.
>
> Then he gets to this.
>
> McLain– “There is no national leadership of Antifa, is there?”
>
> Shideler– “It would be inconsistent with their ideology.”
>
> “Is that a no?”
>
> “It would be inconsistent with their ideology, so they do not, no.”
>
> “OK. They don’t have membership rolls.”
>
> “It would be inconsistent with their ideology, so no.”
>
> “Just for the sake of efficiency, if there is a yes or no answer, could you
> lead with that?”
>
> “Sure.”
>
> “OK. Thank you. And no dues or hierarchy in anything that you would call
> Antifa, right?”
>
> “No, they’re opposed to it.”

So, to summarize: no leadership, no membership, no dues. Shideler goes on to
admit that the members of this supposed cell of a larger organization didn’t
even refer to themselves as “antifa” in their private Signal chats.

The attempt to associate the defendants with this thing called antifa was so
ludicrous that the defense attorneys saw no need to call their own expert
witness. In fact, convinced that the Justice Department had badly screwed the
pooch on the case, the defense didn’t even bother to call any witnesses of
their own.

Having failed to prove the existence of antifa, the prosecution fell back on
the more general charge of “terrorism.” In the spirit of the Sacco and
Vanzetti case (which used “anarchism”) and the Rosenberg case (which used
“communism”), the jury and then the judge threw the book at the hapless eight
because they supposedly served as the pawns of an all-powerful shadowy force.

**Global Ties**

The failure of the Justice Department to prove the existence of antifa
notwithstanding, the Trump administration has worked hard to play up the
threat of this shadowy organization and connect it to other convenient
bogeymen.

If Vladimir Putin weren’t a friend of Trump’s, Russia would no doubt be on the
State Department’s list of antifa supporters because of its Soviet credentials
and its stated goal to root out Nazism in Ukraine. The administration has
sought an economic accommodation with Beijing, so China is out of the picture
as well (though congressional Republicans have nonetheless [gone after other
left-wing groups](https://truthout.org/articles/house-republicans-subpoena-
left-wing-groups-as-trump-admin-assembles-blacklists/ "gone after other left-
wing groups") for their closeness to China).

What remains are [Iran and Cuba](https://theconversation.com/the-trump-
administrations-global-campaign-against-radical-left-terrorism-is-built-on-a-
national-security-memo-without-congressional-approval-287276 "Iran and Cuba"),
which Secretary of State Rubio accuses, without providing any credible
evidence, of supporting the vast left-wing conspiracy. Even if any sort of
connections could be proved among the three—ayatollahs, communist
apparatchiks, and anti-fascist campaigners—it doesn’t add up to much of an
“axis of evil.”

It’s no surprise, then, that the Trump administration has been [unable to
convince anyone](https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-
security/2026/07/09/rubio-tries-enlist-other-nations-antifa-fight-some-allies-
recoil/ "unable to convince anyone") other than itself about this supposed
threat. The State Department held a meeting in The Netherlands in May about
left-wing violence, but it had to be at the U.S. embassy since the Dutch
declined to host the event. In June, a similar gathering at the U.S. Institute
for Peace failed to launch. A request sent by the State Department to a number
of countries for information about antifa didn’t elicit much response. The
four foreign left organizations that have earned the label “terrorist” from
the U.S. government have, at worst, committed some acts of vandalism, and
European countries have by and large rejected the designation.

More interesting than the tortuous arguments deployed by the administration to
pursue its case are the likely reasons and the timing of the campaign. The
United States is at war with Iran, so it’s an obvious candidate for
demonization. The administration has talked of regime change in Cuba—as soon
as it wraps up its war in Iran—so the “antifa” charge is but one of many
placed at the island’s doorstep as a rationale for intervention.

But the real target is the “enemy within.” Trump has been eager to portray the
Democratic Party as extremist, as anti-democratic, as a front for its more
radical members like New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-MN).
It is thus simultaneously preparing an electoral campaign to defeat the
opposition in the November elections and a post-electoral campaign to
marginalize a party likely to win one if not both chambers of Congress.

The open question is whether the administration will use the antifa conspiracy
and the terrorist label to widen the scope of arrests. Trump has demonstrated
a willingness to detain hundreds of thousands of people, some of them U.S.
citizens, in his fervor to whiten the country through mass deportations.
Perhaps the two final years of the administration will be spent sending
members of an imaginary conspiracy to detention centers.

It wouldn’t be the first time that the U.S. government targeted immigrants and
left-wingers in a single campaign. In 1920, for instance, Attorney General A.
Mitchell Palmer ordered the arrest of thousands of people on the suspicion
that they were anarchists or communists and were planning an insurrection
against the U.S. government. Later he warned of assassination plots against
U.S. officials. Many of those arrested were immigrants and, like celebrated
activist Emma Goldman, unceremoniously kicked out of the country.

If it hadn’t been [for the courageous actions of Louis
Post](https://www.saturdayeveningpost.com/2025/05/100-years-ago-the-man-who-
singlehandedly-stopped-thousands-of-illegal-deportations/ "for the courageous
actions of Louis Post"), an assistant labor secretary in the Wilson
administration who was also in charge of immigration, thousands more people
would have been deported. In an administration staffed by the likes of Stephen
Miller and Kash Patel, it might be nearly impossible to find a modern-day
Louis Post to head off any future witch hunt. The obvious alternative is to
put up as many roadblocks to the mass deportation campaign as possible before
it destroys more lives and spreads to other segments of the population.

The post [The Myth of a Global
Antifa](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/08/07/the-myth-of-a-global-antifa/)
appeared first on [CounterPunch.org](https://www.counterpunch.org).
